name: Mixed and prepared meals (frozen dinners, boxed meals, ready-to-eat)
scope_note: Adult and general-population frozen dinners, boxed meals, and ready-to-eat composite meals combining a starch/grain, a protein (meat, poultry, fish or other seafood, including aquatic invertebrates), vegetables, and often legumes/pulses and a dairy component. Infant and toddler mixed meals route to Category 1; a product that is primarily a single matrix (plain pasta, a single vegetable) routes to that matrix category. Bone broth is certified under Category 35 row bone-broth (mechanistically distinct hazard). Principal components for anchor selection are the starch or grain, the meat, poultry, fish or other seafood protein, the vegetables, the pulses or legumes, and the dairy fraction of cream-style and cheese-based variants. DAIRY IS A PRINCIPAL COMPONENT AND ITS CEILINGS ARE IMPORTED. v1.1 excluded dairy on the ground that it 'carries its own Category 24 milk ceilings at the ingredient stage'. That argument is not available, because this row applies the opposite rule to seafood: the seafood component is likewise governed at its own stage by the Category 6 seafood ceilings and its component maximum levels ARE imported into the ladder (fish lead 300, fish total mercury 500, seafood inorganic arsenic 100 and 50). No mass or characterizing test distinguishes the two. The composite convention admits a component when it is a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component of products within the row as scoped, and cream is a major-mass component of a bisque or chowder while cheese is the characterizing component of a macaroni-and-cheese or a cheese-sauced meal, exactly as the fish in a fish pie is. Dairy is therefore ADMITTED, and hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 (Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products, 20 ug/kg lead each) enter the lead component set, which moves the published lead ceiling from 50 to 20 ug/kg. On total mercury the corresponding rows hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10 and hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10 are admitted at 10 ug/kg and tie with the binding vegetable value, so the published mercury ceiling is unchanged. On cadmium, total arsenic, nickel and total chromium no credible regulator publishes a dairy row at all, which is stated here rather than left as a silence. Cap. 132V Note 10 scopes Secondary milk products to products that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, so neither Cap. 132V row directly regulates cream or cheese; the milk value is the nearest applicable sovereign anchor for the dairy component and is adopted by disclosed read-across, which is what every other component on this row does and what Method v2.0 prescribes for an unregulated exact cell. The alternative considered and rejected was narrowing the row to exclude cream-style and cheese-based products; that would contradict this row's own product examples, would strand chowder, bisque and macaroni-and-cheese formats with no certifiable home, and is a Step 0 taxonomy decision rather than a limit-setting one.
material: Multi-component composite food. A starch or grain fraction (rice, pasta, noodle, potato, bread component), a protein fraction (meat, poultry, fish, or aquatic-invertebrate seafood), a vegetable fraction, frequently a pulse or legume fraction, a sauce or gravy fraction, and in cream-style and cheese-based variants a dairy fraction. Presented frozen, chilled, canned, retort-pouched or shelf-stable in a plastic or moulded-fibre tray, a retort pouch, a can, a board carton, or a film-sealed pack, and heated by the consumer in the pack.
components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the whole retail portion homogenised as consumed, after any consumer preparation step named on the pack, is the analytical unit for all eleven panel cells; a composite of not fewer than three retail units per lot, drawn across the lot's run. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED FRACTIONS, required whenever a panel result on the homogenate is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation, so the source can be located rather than inferred: the starch or grain fraction, the protein fraction, the vegetable fraction, the pulse or legume fraction, the sauce or gravy fraction, and the dairy fraction. (3) SEAFOOD REFLEX: on any lot whose formulation contains fish or an aquatic invertebrate, the seafood fraction is retained for reflex methylmercury speciation (MeHg control cell) and reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation, and is analysed whenever total mercury or total arsenic on the homogenate approaches the published ceiling. (4) PACKAGING AND CONTACT SURFACES, which are the escalation targets for the aluminium and tin controls rather than routine analytical units: the tray or pouch and its lidding film or laminate, foil components, the can where the form is canned, and the aluminium cookware and contact surfaces of the production line. (5) INGREDIENT WATER, verified on specification against the applicable national drinking-water standard rather than by analysis of the composite.
basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed in Cap 132V|as_sold
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary food maximum level in a comparable as-consumed family (EU wet weight or product as placed on the market, FSANZ portion ordinarily consumed, Cap. 132V food as sold). The guard stops a drinking-water parametric value, an animal-feed maximum, a food-contact-material specific migration limit, or a toy migration limit from silently anchoring a composite food cell: those are different basis classes and are not comparable to a food-content ceiling. A cell whose named anchor falls outside the family fails the build instead of publishing a mixed-basis number. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GUARD ACTUALLY DOES, corrected in v1.2: it refuses the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada drinking-water instruments, the EU 10/2011 specific migration limits, animal-feed maxima, and toy migration limits, because each carries a distinct basis string. It does NOT refuse the Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows, which share the single Cap. 132V basis string with that instrument's food rows and are therefore indistinguishable to a basis regex. Those rows are excluded by the stated ingredient-water determination and are named by id in each affected cell's companion set, not silently dropped.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: the dairy component binds at 20 ug/kg (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, Milk and Secondary milk products), stricter than the fruiting-vegetable and preserved-tomato rows (50 each) that bound in v1.1 and stricter than the root/tuber vegetable (100), meat (100), cereal (200) and fish (300) components. Tightened from 100 to 50 in v1.1 on the Cap. 132V admission, and from 50 to 20 in v1.2 on the dairy ruling
Pb.substantiation: THE BINDING MOVED IN v1.2 BECAUSE THE DAIRY EXCLUSION DID NOT SURVIVE AUDIT. The ruling, the test that produced it, and the rejected alternatives are stated in full in this row's scope_note; in short, no mass or characterizing test distinguishes cream in a bisque or cheese in a macaroni-and-cheese from the seafood, meat and vegetable components already imported, so hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 are admitted and the ceiling is 20 ug/kg. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a meal whose characterizing component is a cereal (Cap. 132V and FSANZ cereal lead 200) or a fish (EU 300) contains a component whose own sovereign ceiling is up to fifteen times this composite ceiling, so such a product may measure above it. That does not loosen the ceiling; the component is governed at its own stage by its own category, and a composite lot above 20 ug/kg lead is not certifiable on this row. The v1.1 ladder is retained and unchanged below the new binding: Cap. 132V sets lead at 50 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables (cucurbit and non-cucurbit alike) and for tomatoes preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed, which is the canned tomato base of most sauced prepared meals. Two stricter Cap. 132V lead rows remain deliberately NOT adopted and are now equal to rather than stricter than the binding: cereal-based food (20 ug/kg) and ready-to-eat complementary food other than cereal-based (20 ug/kg), both scoped to persons under the age of 36 months. This row certifies adult and general-population meals only; infant and toddler mixed meals route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, so an under-36-months action level is not an applicable anchor here, and the Codex ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children ML (20 ug/kg) is dispositioned identically. Leafy-vegetable lead MLs (EU 2023/915 and Cap. 132V, 300 ug/kg each) and the fish ML (300) are applicable but looser and are disclosed rather than adopted. BEVERAGE-COMMODITY RULING, applied once and consistently across every analyte on this row. Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant lead row below 20 ug/kg returns only drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (5 to 10 ug/kg) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard as different basis families. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

tAs.label: Cap. 132V sets a total-arsenic ML of 500 ug/kg for vegetables, for cereals other than rice, for meat of animal and for meat of poultry, which covers every principal component of a mixed meal and is stricter than the FSANZ cereal-grain ML (1000) that v1.0 selected. Total arsenic is published as a protective sovereign maximum level, not as a screen; the health-relevant inorganic fraction is separately and more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: TOTAL ARSENIC IS PUBLISHED HERE AS A PROTECTIVE SOVEREIGN MAXIMUM LEVEL, NOT AS A SCREEN. v1.1 opened this substantiation with 'Total arsenic is a non-toxicological screen' while the cell emitted an ordinary numeric read-across with no screen flag, so the prose and the provenance disagreed about whether the published number was protective and any renderer that distinguishes the two would have contradicted the cell's own text. The disagreement is resolved in favour of what the cell in fact publishes: Cap. 132V regulates total arsenic as a per-commodity protective ceiling, 500 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum level for the components of this row, and it is published as such. Total arsenic is one of the eight mandatory HMTc totals and is never satisfied by its species. The screen mechanism (`screen: true` with a screen_note) is used on this config only for total chromium, where the published value genuinely is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling; it is not available on a component_read_across cell in this compiler in any case. The toxicologically dominant arsenic species, inorganic arsenic, is separately and far more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg (EU 2025/1891 cephalopods), and the species-below-total relation holds (iAs 50 <= tAs 500). v1.1 tightens the cell from 1000 to 500 ug/kg because the Cap. 132V per-commodity total-arsenic MLs reach the components for which the FSANZ cereal-grain ML was the only anchor, and the v1.0 claim that cereal grains carry the only credible total-arsenic component ML is withdrawn. Rice is deliberately absent from Cap. 132V's total-arsenic schedule because rice is regulated on inorganic arsenic instead; that is handled on the iAs cell and never by letting a species stand in for a total. The Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils total-arsenic ML (100 ug/kg) is stricter still and is NOT adopted: cooking fat is a minor formulation ingredient rather than a characterizing component of a meal, edible oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis, and holding a whole meal to an oil ceiling would import a limit from a material that is a few percent of the product. Food-grade salt (500) is dispositioned the same way, as an ingredient specification rather than a composite ceiling. The stricter rung is adopted, the equal rungs are named, and the looser rungs are disclosed and not adopted. tHg.label: the vegetable total-mercury ML (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 10 ug/kg) binds. v1.1 replaces the v1.0 seafood-only anchor of 500 ug/kg: Cap. 132V does set mercury MLs for the terrestrial components of a mixed meal (vegetables 10, rice/maize/wheat and their flours 20, meat of animal 50, meat of poultry 50, poultry eggs 50), and vegetables are a principal component of essentially every product in this row.
tHg.substantiation: The v1.0 statement that no credible regulator sets a mercury maximum level for terrestrial meat, cereals or vegetables was true only while Hong Kong sat outside the credible-regulator set. Cap. 132V was admitted on 2026-08-17, and its Part 2 Schedule item for mercury (expressed as total mercury) sets 10 ug/kg for vegetables other than edible fungi, 20 for rice, maize and wheat and their flours, and 50 for meat of animal, meat of poultry and poultry eggs. The strictest applicable component therefore moves this cell from 500 to 10 ug/kg, a fifty-fold tightening, and the false claim is corrected rather than preserved. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a seafood-characterized composite (tuna casserole, fish pie, prawn stir-fry) contains a component whose own sovereign ceiling is 500 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 fish; Cap. 132V aquatic animals other than fish, 500), so such a product will frequently measure above this composite ceiling. That does not loosen the ceiling. The seafood ingredient is governed at its own stage by the Category 6 seafood ceilings, a composite lot above 10 ug/kg total mercury is not certifiable on this row, and whether a seafood-characterized composite warrants its own taxonomy row is a Step 0 category decision rather than a limit-setting decision. v1.2 admits the dairy component under the ruling stated in this row's scope_note; Cap. 132V sets total mercury at 10 ug/kg for Milk (hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10) and for Secondary milk products (hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10), which ties the binding vegetable value, so dairy is named in the component set and the published ceiling is unchanged at 10 ug/kg. Edible fungi (Cap. 132V 100 ug/kg) are applicable but looser and are disclosed rather than adopted. Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by this total (MeHg <= tHg) and is handled on the MeHg cell. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. MeHg.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: authors2025-the-icp-ms-study-on-the-release-of and hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury in this matrix, so the species is not absent and no not-material determination is supportable. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling of 10 ug/kg for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented. INSTRUMENTS CHECKED, so the negative claim is auditable: EU 2023/915 (no methylmercury entry); Codex CXS 193 (none); FSANZ Schedule 19 (none); Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (none); US FDA CPG 540.600, which sets a methylmercury action level of 1000 ug/kg for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals but not for a composite meal; and HK Cap. 132V, whose methylmercury rows are fish-species rows (fish, fish balls and fish cakes 500; orange roughy 800; pink cusk-eel 1000; tuna 1200; alfonsino 1500; shark 1600; marlin 1700 ug/kg). Every existing value is an aquatic-animal instrument and every one is looser than the 10 ug/kg total-mercury ceiling published on this row, so none could bind even if it were applicable. EVIDENCE TEST, AND WHY THE TWO COMPOSITE ROWS OF THIS CATEGORY RESOLVE METHYLMERCURY DIFFERENTLY. hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury directly in 480 Korean home-meal-replacement products and reported it BY MATRIX PHASE: detected in the non-fatty solid phase (mean 3.0, maximum 48.0 ug/kg) and the fatty solid phase, and NOT DETECTED in both the non-fatty liquid phase and the fatty liquid phase. A soup, broth or stock is the liquid phase, and a plated frozen dinner is the solid phase. That is why mixed-meals-prepared-foods holds methylmercury under mandatory analytical control (the species was measured in its matrix, so a not-material determination is not supportable there) while this row records a substantiated not-material determination with a reflex trigger. The asymmetry is evidence-driven and is recorded here rather than left to look like an inconsistency. Occurrence evidence is used only to test materiality, never to select a number (Method v2.0).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by closed-vessel acid digestion with ICP-MS or CV-AAS on the homogenised as-consumed composite; reflex methylmercury speciation (species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS) only on a seafood-containing meal whose total mercury approaches the total-mercury ceiling.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate/canned-food migration pathway, not a background dietary contaminant of a frozen or boxed meal. A CANNED prepared meal (canned ravioli, canned chili) is governed by the canned-foods tin ML (Codex CXS 193, 250 mg/kg = 250000 ug/kg); a frozen, chilled, or dry-packaged prepared meal has no tin source. Total tin is reported; a signal on a non-canned form triggers packaging-source investigation. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS; canned forms verified against the canned-foods tin ML.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for a prepared meal or for any principal component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, which are Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in three basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011, a migration figure), and toy migration limits. Permitted-additive maxima for aluminium-containing additives in baked goods and starch noodles exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels rather than contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed composite, one determination per production lot, reported on the certificate with no numeric pass/fail. Escalation: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of aluminium cookware and contact surfaces, foil and laminate packaging, and any aluminium-containing additive in the formulation, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a cooked, wet, organic-rich food matrix: it is reduced to trivalent chromium (Cr-III) by the food's reducing environment during cooking and digestion. A Cr-VI result in prepared food is a measurement artifact of the total-chromium screen, not a real exposure. No credible regulator sets a Cr-VI food ML.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Cr-VI is not measured routinely; total chromium (Cr cell) is the reported screen and bounds any hexavalent fraction.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food; Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a cooked, wet, organic-rich matrix and any Cr(VI) signal is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V — none set a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
